title: Session composition & tool-handshake scratchpad (WIP)
content:
Overview:
This doc is a working scratchpad exploring an alternative approach to session composition and progressive tool-handshake semantics for the Hosted API SDKs. Goal: make partial results first-class (parsable JSON fragments), support multi-device resumable sessions, and give SDKs a simple progressive handshake that minimizes blocking and improves mobile/edge UX.

Context / problem statement:
- Customers integrate heavy tool-chaining flows (search -> tool -> enrichment -> compose) and need predictable incremental results for UI updates.
- Current streaming model emits token deltas optimized for latency but leaves a lot of app-level reassembly to customers.
- Tool calling today is synchronous or full response-based which contributes to head-of-line blocking and fragile retries.
- Mobile apps in low-bandwidth scenarios need resumable partial snapshots (so a user can resume on a different device or recover after an intermittent network).

High-level design ideas (brainstorm):
1) Session composition primitives
   - session_id: server-managed opaque id returned at start-of-session.
   - epoch sequence: incremental numeric epoch for every committed checkpoint from the runtime.
   - checkpoint frames: compact delta snapshots of structured output and tool-call state (JSON-lines friendly).
   - event journal: append-only stream of semantic events (e.g., tool:invoke, tool:returned, partial:json-frame). Events are small and idempotent.

2) Progressive tool handshake (low-latency handshake phases)
   - Phase 0: declare-intent: client sends a light schema for expected tool outputs and preferred fallback (e.g., text-only fallback, dry-run). Server acknowledges capabilities.
   - Phase 1: pre-resolve: server optionally resolves quick metadata (tool availability, estimated ETA) and emits a pre-resolve event.
   - Phase 2: tool-execution-stream: tool calls stream partial structured frames as they become available (streamed JSON frames, each with an event_id and stable operation id).
   - Phase 3: commit-or-abort: final commit event marks tool completion; clients can request a replay from last commit.

3) Partial-JSON framing and SDK ergonomics
   - Use lightweight JSON-Lines (ndjson) frames with a small header: {"type": "frame", "epoch": 12, "op": "tool-output", "id": "op-234", "payload": {...}}
   - SDKs expose iterator-style readFrames() returning typed events; high-level helpers map frames to domain objects (messages, toolResults, attachments).
   - Provide an 'applyPatch' utility that takes the last committed snapshot and an incoming delta frame and returns a merged snapshot. This keeps app code concise.

4) Resumable sessions & offline snapshots
   - Checkpoints are small (diffs) and can be persisted by the SDK locally (encrypted). On reconnect, SDK offers resume(session_id, last_epoch). Server validates and sends missing events.
   - For cross-device resume, user tokens should permit resume-only scopes tied to session id (short TTL).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- SDK streaming API can surface partial structured tool output in a typed manner (JS/TS and Python).
- Server emits stable session_id and epoched checkpoints; SDK can resume after transient network loss and reconstruct final result.
- Tool handshake phases reduce median time-to-first-structured-frame by 30% in our mobile simulation (slow 3G emulation).
- Backwards-compatible: clients that ignore frames still get final completed payloads.

Telemetry & metrics to track:
- time_to_first_frame_by_platform (mobile/web/server)
- resume_success_rate and resume_replay_latency
- average_checkpoint_size and number_of_checkpoints_per_session
- tool_handshake_fail_rate and pre-resolve_hit_rate
- SDK-level telemetry: frames_applied_success, patch_conflict_count

API surface (sketches):
- REST/HTTP: POST /v1/sessions -> {model, instructions, client_capabilities} returns {session_id, initial_frame} (streamable).
- Stream frames over SSE/HTTP2 or WebSocket with framing type header 'x-rw-frame: ndjson'.
- SDK JS snippet (idea):
  const s = await client.sessions.start({model, schema});
  for await (const f of s.streamFrames()) {
    if (f.type === 'tool-output') ui.patch(f.payload);
    if (f.type === 'checkpoint') localStore.save(s.id, f.epoch, f.payload);
  }
  // resume
  const r = await client.sessions.resume(sessionId, {lastEpoch: 12});

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should session_id be user-readable or opaque? Opaque simplifies security but makes debugging harder.
- Checkpoint frequency vs. cost: more frequent = better resume UX, worse cost and storage. Need heuristics (time-since-last-checkpoint or major-state-change triggers).
- Privacy: storing checkpoints locally may capture PII. SDK must default to encrypted storage and provide opt-outs.
- Consistency model: eventual consistency across checkpoints; do we need causal guarantees across parallel tool fanouts? (probably not for MVP).

Migration story for existing users:
- Keep final-response compatibility. New streaming frames are additive; older SDKs will ignore frames and still get final payload.
- Provide a migration helper library that translates token-delta streams into approximate JSON frames for a transitional period.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Alpha: internal SDKs + 2 pilot customers; collect resume metrics, patch conflicts, and telemetry.
- Beta: broader SDK release, enable opt-in via feature flag, provide migration guide and a small CLI to inspect sessions.
- GA: enabled by default with bookkeeping quotas and an admin console to view sessions/checkpoints.

Risks & mitigations:
- Storage growth from persisted checkpoints -> add retention policies, delta compaction, and per-customer quotas.
- Complex SDK surface -> ship minimal helpers first (streamFrames, resume) and iterate on ergonomics.
- Tool-call security boundaries -> require explicit tool scopes and signatures for cross-tenant tool outputs.

Implementation notes (infra & runtime):
- Runtime needs a lightweight journal per-session (S3-backed append log or Kafka topics per shard).
- Checkpointing should be offloaded to an async worker that compacts recent events into a small snapshot.
- Use existing routing/fallback policies to map tool calls to dedicated capacity when available.

TODOs (me & team):
- [ ] Prototype ndjson frame serializer and small JS helper (Ravi)
- [ ] Mobile resume flow UX spec (Elena)
- [ ] Instrumentation plan and dashboards (Jon)
- [ ] POC of server-side journal compaction and replay API (infra)
- [ ] Security review for persisted checkpoints (security & compliance)

Notes to self / discussion crumbs:
- Consider a lightweight 'replay token' concept for ephemeral cross-device resumes. Could be tied to session start and revocable.
- For very long sessions, consider epoch quanta (e.g., group every 100 events into a compaction).
- Slack thread: #hosted-api-streaming has ongoing debate about JSON-lines vs typed binary frames. Keep both options in mind; JSON-lines wins for debuggability.

Related artifacts / links:
- prototype: github:repo/hosted-sdk/tree/session-proto (work-in-progress)
- jira: HOSTEDAPI-723 (session resume epic)
- confluence: Hosted API streaming primitives (internal spec link)

If this doc looks reasonable I'll flesh out an explicit PRD with sequence diagrams, a small SDK API RFC, and a rollout checklist. For now this is intentionally light on final decisions and heavy on tradeoffs.

-- Maya
